context:
Keep the change focused on bundle loading. Do not touch the DuckDB
attach logic, the fixture generator, or the range-read test server -
those are separate concerns owned by other TODOs.
description:
The explorer no longer bootstraps DuckDB-WASM from jsDelivr. Instead,
`results-explorer/src/lib/duckdbBundles.ts` imports the worker and WASM
assets directly from the installed npm package via Vite `?url` imports,
and `results-explorer/src/db.ts` now resolves the runtime bundle from
that same-origin descriptor.

This removed the external CDN dependency for both production explorer
loads and the browser-functional harness without introducing a separate
committed vendor directory. Because the browser now imports assets from
the installed package at build time, there is no duplicated byte copy to
desync from `package-lock.json`.

anti_patterns.dont: commit the WASM binaries into `results-explorer/public/vendor/duckdb-wasm/` without a desync guard
anti_patterns.instead: wire in the version check in the same PR that vendors the bundle.
anti_patterns.why: `npm install` can silently drift the runtime version away from the shipped WASM bytes

anti_patterns.dont: remove the jsDelivr fallback without confirming the vendored path handles the MVP / EH / COI worker variants the way `selectBundle` does
anti_patterns.instead: exercise `selectBundle` against the vendored descriptor first, then drop jsDelivr only if every platform target still resolves to a local file.
anti_patterns.why: picking the wrong variant silently degrades performance or breaks threading

preserves.behavior: Cross-origin isolation (COEP/COOP) still enables SharedArrayBuffer in the browser.
The Chromium blocking gate keeps passing throughout the change.
`registerFileURL('results.duckdb', ...)` and `ATTACH ... AS bench (READ_ONLY)` continue to work unchanged - this TODO only moves bundle loading, not file registration.

verifications.description: The TODO item itself validates cleanly
verifications.expected: Validation passes with no schema or DAG errors

verifications.description: Chromium e2e suite passes with jsDelivr network access blocked
verifications.expected: Smoke suite passes with no jsDelivr requests observed in the network log

work_units.notes:
Added `results-explorer/src/lib/duckdbBundles.ts` with MVP/EH/COI
asset descriptors and switched `results-explorer/src/db.ts` to use
`selectBundle(LOCAL_DUCKDB_BUNDLES)`.
work_units.summary: Load the duckdb-wasm bundle from same-origin Vite asset URLs

work_units.notes:
Added a smoke assertion in
`results-explorer/e2e/smoke/harness.spec.ts` that fails on any
request to `cdn.jsdelivr.net`.
work_units.summary: Assert in smoke coverage that e2e no longer hits jsDelivr

work_units.notes:
Vite now emits the worker/WASM assets directly from
`node_modules/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm`, so there is no separate
vendored directory to drift from the lockfile.
work_units.summary: Keep bundle bytes in lockstep with the installed npm package
